text:
Natalie: Ran the RC perf suite; synthetic harness OK, but replay shows a persistent tail and ~25% higher p95.

Sanjay: share the exact harness flags? connection reuse and socket options matter.

Natalie: replay cmd:
```
./perf-harness replay --trace traces/2026-03-11.prod --clients 48 --qps 220 --reuse-connections=false
```
I disabled reuse to simulate heavy mobile churn.

Zoe: big mismatch — synthetic driver defaults to reuse-connections=true. apples vs oranges.

Mario: also check TCP_NODELAY and TLS session resumption. New TLS handshakes + small writes can collide with Nagle.

Natalie: reran with `--reuse-connections=true --tcp-nodelay=true`: short sequences matched baseline; long contexts still noisy.

Eli: profiler during 2048-token spike?

Natalie: perf snapshot:
```
12.0% runtime attention_kernel_avx512
10.5% runtime matmul_kernel_avx2
9.1% runtime kv_cache_lookup
6.4% runtime cuda_memcpy
```
Looks like kernel selection picks AVX512 for long seqs, but the AVX512 path falls back to a scalar loop for some head sizes and is slower.

Sanjay: kernel-selection heuristic too eager. Need calibration using real seq distributions and observed per-token times, not just seq len.

Zoe: batching makes this worse: our batcher grows with qps and avg seq len but ignores kv_hit_rate. Batching many cold long-requests multiplies latency.

Mario: idea: KV-aware batching. If kv_hit_rate < 0.9, cap batch size (e.g., max 4) and prioritize short-context into larger batches.

Natalie: quick prototype config:
```
batcher:
  max_batch: 32
  kv_adaptive: true
  kv_hit_threshold: 0.9
  max_on_miss: 4
```
Replay with KV-adaptive: p95 down ~18%, throughput -6%, latency SLO met.

Eli: we should log selected kernel per request and aggregate per-run to correlate with seq hist and kv metrics.

Sanjay: client semantics matter: gRPC multiplexes streams on few TCP connections (masks handshake churn) but can create head-of-line blocking for long token streams. REST clients often use more short-lived connections unless explicitly configured.

Zoe: propose an apples-to-apples test matrix: reuse on/off, TLS resumption on/off, tcp_nodelay toggles, gRPC vs HTTP, kv warm/cold, seq histogram.

Natalie: adding checklist to PR and infra docs.

Mario: FYI Java bench client default socket opts added ~7ms tail in a customer run; ensure all bench clients toggle TCP_NODELAY.

Eli: measurement tips: include warmup and drop first N minutes of data; capture kernel-selection time series and kv hit ratio.

infra-bot: CI change: exporting runtime.kv_hit_rate; nightly job perf/replay-kv-aware added (runs both reuse modes + protocols).

Natalie: next steps: kernel-selection calibration PR to compare AVX512 vs AVX2 across head sizes/seq combos and back off AVX512 when per-token cost higher.

Sanjay: sounds good. Also add eng-runtime doc "bench apples-to-apples checklist" with example perf-harness invocation and KV-adaptive batcher snippet.

Zoe: I'll draft and ping here. thanks :thumbsup:
